testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When starting down a hill, you should shift into a ____ gear.
questions.explanation: Before going downhill, shift into a low gear. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as you travel downhill.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks and the air brake system from too much air pressure. It usually opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: When traveling down a steep downgrade:

options.text: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
Continually downshift instead of using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put the vehicle in a low gear and use engine braking.
questions.explanation: On long or steep downgrades, use engine braking to control your speed. Use your brakes only to help with this.

questions.question: An alcohol evaporator in an air brake system:

options.text: Makes the brakes work without squeaking.
Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
Lubricates parts of the braking system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents ice from forming in the braking system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an evaporator that adds alcohol to the system. The alcohol helps prevent ice from forming in the system.

questions.question: A dual air brake system:

options.text: Has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
Is one air brake system with two different sets of controls.
Has one system for the left side and one for the right side, each with its own controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: Has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. They share one set of brake controls, but each has its own air tanks, hoses, and lines. One system usually operates the brakes on the rear axle while the other operates the brakes on the front axle.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: An air compressor governor controls:

options.text: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
How fast air is pumped into the storage tanks.
The temperature of the air pumped into the storage tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the air compressor pumps air into the storage tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor controls when the air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks.

questions.question: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have ____ malfunction lamps to show when ABS is not working.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow malfunction lamps to alert drivers when the braking systems are not working. Know where the malfunction lamp is on your vehicle before you start driving.

questions.question: Having ABS on only one axle:

options.text: Still gives you more control when braking.
Slows the vehicle, but cannot stop it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still gives you more control when braking.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has ABS on only the tractor, trailer, or one axle, you will still have more control when braking than without ABS. Brake normally.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in an air brake system contains water and oil. These can damage the system if they build up. Air tanks have drain valves to remove water and oil from the compressed air.

questions.question: What should air tank drains be used for?

options.text: They should not be used by the driver.
They should only be used when it is wet outside.
They should drain the tanks completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: They should drain the tanks completely.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. These can damage the brakes if they build up in the system. You must open the manual drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Is a low air pressure warning signal required on vehicles with air brakes?
questions.explanation: Any vehicle with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal.

questions.question: What should be done with water and compressor oil found in air brake systems?

options.text: They are necessary for the system to work properly.
They should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and compressor oil can damage air brake systems if they build up. Air storage tanks have drains to remove this buildup. Open the manual drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: What causes brake fade?
questions.explanation: When brakes are overused, they get too hot. This heat causes them to fade and become less effective at slowing the vehicle.

questions.question: In vehicles with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank do?

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: In vehicles with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can temporarily release spring brakes if they have been activated due to low air pressure. Push the proper control to release the spring brakes for a short time. This lets you move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: What do air storage tanks do?

options.text: They are not allowed on vehicles.
They hold compressed air for the brakes.
They should be drained of excess air after every trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: They hold compressed air for the brakes.
questions.explanation: In air brake systems, air storage tanks hold compressed air for the brakes to use. The number and size of tanks varies by vehicle.

questions.question: Where are foundation brakes used on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Foundation brakes are used on every wheel of a vehicle. The most common type is the s-cam drum brake.

questions.question: What color are anti-lock brake warning lights?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have yellow warning lights that show when there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: How must an emergency brake be controlled?
questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. Air pressure can leak away over time, so emergency and parking brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, how much distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance for air brake vehicles has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: In cold weather, check your vehicle's alcohol evaporator:
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in air brake systems. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and have the brakes fixed within a week.
Pull over and check the brakes.
Call a mechanic while you drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and check the brakes.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on while driving a vehicle with air brakes, stop safely as soon as you can while you still have brake control. Check and repair the brakes right away.

questions.question: What is commonly found in compressed air?
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems usually contains water and compressor oil. Water and oil can damage the brakes if they build up. Drain tanks regularly to remove this buildup.

questions.question: If the air compressor has a belt, you should regularly check that it is:
questions.explanation: If your vehicle has air brakes, check the compressor belt before each drive. Make sure the belt is tight and in good condition.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the pedal
The distance between the brake pedal and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The time it takes for brakes to work after you press the pedal
questions.explanation: Air brakes cannot work instantly because air takes time to travel through the lines to the brakes. There is usually a brake lag of at least half a second between pressing the pedal and the brakes starting to work.
